This comprehensive review should include a review of all relevant in-process and finished product data obtained by your firm including all batch records. An interim plan for risk mitigation while you perform broader studies to improve your visual inspection program. Provide a detailed list of your risk mitigations (e.g., sampling plans and methods for your proposed destructive testing). 4. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). There was a pattern of inadequate investigations into critical issues, including leaking drug products and sterility failures. Leaking Units Your investigations into the “systemic nature” of container-closure integrity failures lacked effective CAPA to address the significantly increased rate of leak defects in your injectable drug products. You did not implement sufficient CAPA to ensure remediation of your final inspection program. Further, since 2023, media fill units were found leaking during incubation and you have received numerous leak complaints for marketed products. All sterile drugs must be packaged using container-closure systems with robust protection that prevents the ingress of microorganisms. A product’s ability to maintain integrity throughout anticipated stresses and external factors during manufacture, storage, distribution, and consumer use is critical to ensure product quality and safety. Loss of container-closure integrity is a direct cause of non-sterility. In your response, you acknowledge that strengthening your investigation system is warranted and you will evaluate whether (b)(4) container closure integrity testing (CCIT) could be an effective layered control. You also commit to a retrospective review of critical non-conformance reports (NCR) and laboratory investigations for the last year. Your response is inadequate. Limiting a retrospective review to (b)(4) lacks adequate scientific justification as your leak trending data illustrated the leak rate has consistently increased annually from 2023 to 2026. You also do not sufficiently address how a lack of highly capable leak detection systems impacts already produced products, or sufficiently detail improvements to your CAPA system. In addition, data from your firm indicates that although leak rate has increased, the number of NCRs opened has decreased. Sterility Failure Your investigation into a 2025 sterility failure for cefazolin, lot (b)(4) , assigned the root cause as a non-integral test container. Test records had been signed and dated indicating that container integrity was initially verified. However, after observing turbidity, you subsequently stated in your investigation that container integrity was not verified, classifying it as a “no-test.” Without conducting a Phase II investigation, you concluded there was no risk to the manufacturing process or finished product. You invalidated the sterility result without adequate scientific justification and released this lot in July 2025. Notably, the same container integrity problem had been observed in the sterility test of (b)(4) , lot (b)(4) , in (b)(4) , which you rejected. In addition, a “no-test” designation was used for an (b)(4) cycle requalification attempt that resulted in numerous positive BIs. In your response, you state your belief that the laboratory error of incubating non-integral sterility test containers was the definitive root cause. Your response is inadequate as it fails to address why your lab records described the test container as integral. It also fails to thoroughly address the lack of contemporaneous documentation of any subsequent deviation that could have theoretically occurred. You also commit to implementing a closed membrane sterility testing system in the future, but your proposal does not ensure timely remediation. Product contamination may go undetected for substantial periods if your firm employs unreliable sterility testing practices. It should also be noted that any positive sterility test result represents a serious CGMP issue that requires a comprehensive investigation into the cause and extent of the problem, and a prompt review of the qualification status of the aseptic process. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. For guidance on establishing and maintaining CGMP-compliant quality systems, see FDA guidance documents: Q8(R2) Pharmaceutical Development at https://www.fda.gov/media/71535/download, Q9(R1) Quality Risk Management at https://www.fda.gov/media/167721/download, and Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System at https://www.fda.gov/media/71553/download. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority, independence, and resources to effectively function. The assessment should also include, but not be limited to, the following: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for independent QU oversight throughout your CGMP operations to ensure satisfactory procedures and adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision, including all investigations o Oversight and approval of discharging of all QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products o Also, describe how executive management supports robust quality assurance at your firm, including, but not limited to, timely provision of resources that enable proactive detection and resolution of emerging manufacturing/quality issues to assure a continuing state of control A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, out-of-specifi

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm manufactures over-the-counter (OTC) drug products such as (b)(4) and (b)(4) , primarily distributed by your customers as promotional items. Your firm routinely failed to investigate out-of-specification (OOS) chemical and microbiological results for drug products and for (b)(4) system monitoring samples. Your firm retested failing samples or prepared and tested new samples without justification until your analysts obtained passing results. Your firm used these results to release drug product to the market without appropriate investigations into the original failing results. Additionally, your firm failed to conduct adequate complaint investigations. Your investigations consisted largely of email correspondence and lacked proper root cause determination and implementation of corrective actions and preventive actions (CAPA). Inadequate investigations are a repeat observation identified at your firm.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 배치 또는 그 구성 성분이 규격에 부합하지 않는 원인불명의 불일치나 부적합에 대해, 해당 배치의 출하 여부와 관계없이 철저히 조사하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.192). 귀사는 주로 고객사가 판촉물로 배포하는 (b)(4) 및 (b)(4) 등 일반의약품(OTC)을 제조한다. 귀사는 의약품과 (b)(4) 시스템 모니터링 시료의 화학적·미생물학적 규격외(OOS) 결과를 일상적으로 조사하지 않았다. 귀사는 분석자가 적합 결과를 얻을 때까지 타당한 근거 없이 부적합 시료를 재시험하거나 새 시료를 조제해 시험했다. 귀사는 최초 부적합 결과에 대한 적절한 조사 없이 이렇게 얻은 결과를 근거로 의약품을 시장에 출하했다. 또한 귀사는 불만 조사를 적절히 수행하지 않았다. 조사는 대부분 이메일 교신으로 이루어졌고, 적절한 근본 원인 규명과 시정 및 예방 조치(CAPA) 이행이 결여되어 있었다. 부적절한 조사는 귀사에서 반복 지적된 사항이다.
key_violations.risk: 부적합 원인을 규명하지 않은 채 재시험 적합 결과로 출하하면 품질 결함 제품이 시장에 유통될 수 있고, 반복 지적이라 FDA의 신뢰 저하가 가중된다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to establish laboratory controls that include scientifically sound and appropriate specifications, standards, sampling plans, and test procedures designed to assure that components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, labeling, and drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b)). Your test method procedures allowed multiple retesting of samples following an OOS result, often until an acceptable result is obtained. For example, your (b)(4) standard operating procedure (SOP) described repreparing OOS samples and retesting multiple times without requiring investigations. The SOP requires notifying quality control management only after (b)(4) OOS results. Your procedure also stated that if an unidentified peak is observed during chromatographic analysis, it is at the discretion of the analyst to consult the Quality Control manager to determine whether further action is needed. Additionally, your (b)(4) Microbial Testing SOP allows retesting following an initial failure. Also, your SOP says that if the retest fails, your analysts are to use the (b)(4) , a second microbiological testing instrument. You routinely invalidated failing batch release results from the (b)(4) system and used the passing (b)(4) results to release product to the market without scientific justification. You could not provide any data to support this tiered testing approach or the validation of one method as superior to the other.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 원료, 의약품 용기, 마개, 공정 중 물질, 표시자재 및 의약품이 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)의 적절한 기준에 부합함을 보증하도록 설계된, 과학적으로 타당하고 적절한 규격·표준품·검체 채취 계획·시험 절차를 포함하는 시험실 관리를 수립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.160(b)). 귀사의 시험법 절차는 OOS 결과 이후 시료를 여러 차례 재시험하는 것을 허용했고, 흔히 허용 가능한 결과가 나올 때까지 재시험했다. 예를 들어 귀사의 (b)(4) 표준작업절차서(SOP)는 조사 요구 없이 OOS 시료를 다시 조제해 여러 차례 재시험하는 방법을 기술했다. 이 SOP는 (b)(4) 번의 OOS 결과가 나온 뒤에야 품질관리 책임자에게 통보하도록 요구한다. 또한 절차서는 크로마토그래피 분석 중 미확인 피크가 관찰되면 추가 조치 필요 여부를 정하기 위해 품질관리 책임자와 상의할지를 분석자 재량에 맡겼다. 아울러 귀사의 (b)(4) 미생물 시험 SOP는 최초 부적합 후 재시험을 허용한다. 또한 SOP는 재시험이 부적합이면 분석자가 두 번째 미생물 시험 장비인 (b)(4)를 사용하도록 한다. 귀사는 (b)(4) 시스템의 배치 출하 부적합 결과를 일상적으로 무효화하고, 과학적 근거 없이 (b)(4)의 적합 결과를 사용해 제품을 시장에 출하했다. 귀사는 이 단계적 시험 방식이나 한 방법이 다른 방법보다 우월하다는 밸리데이션을 뒷받침하는 어떤 데이터도 제시하지 못했다.
key_violations.risk: 재시험·장비 교체로 적합 결과를 고르는 구조는 OOS 은폐와 데이터 무결성 훼손으로 이어져, 미생물 오염 등 부적합 제품의 출하를 막지 못할 수 있다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product. Your firm also failed to validate and establish the reliability of your component supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) and 211.84(d)(2)). You failed to perform adequate identity testing of incoming components used in the manufacture of your OTC drug products. You also failed to collect representative samples from each lot of components. In some cases, you relied on identity test results from previously tested component lots when receiving new shipments of the same component lot. Additionally, you failed to establish the reliability of your suppliers’ certificates of analyses (COAs) at appropriate intervals and accepted COAs without confirmatory testing.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 의약품 각 구성 원료의 확인을 위한 시험을 최소 1개 이상 실시하지 않았다. 또한 귀사는 원료 공급업체 시험 분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 검증·확립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) 및 211.84(d)(2)). 귀사는 OTC 의약품 제조에 사용되는 입고 원료에 대해 적절한 확인시험을 수행하지 않았다. 또한 원료 각 로트에서 대표 검체를 채취하지 않았다. 일부 경우에는 같은 원료 로트의 새 입고분을 받을 때 이전에 시험한 원료 로트의 확인시험 결과에 의존했다. 아울러 귀사는 공급업체 시험성적서(COA)의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 확립하지 않았고, 확인 시험 없이 COA를 수용했다.
key_violations.risk: 입고 원료의 확인시험과 COA 신뢰성 검증이 없으면 오원료·부적합 원료가 제조에 투입되어도 걸러낼 과학적 근거가 없다.

key_violations.original: Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your QU failed to establish and exercise its authority to adequately oversee the manufacturing, testing, packing, holding, review, and release of your OTC drug products. Your firm’s inadequate quality oversight resulted in significant deficiencies in analytical and production record review, investigations, and quality system controls to ensure compliance with CGMP requirements. For example, your QU failed to ensure: Adequate procedures ensuring appropriate document controls of production and test records. (21 CFR 211.22(d)). Adequate validation of cleaning procedures (21 CFR 211.67(b)). Performance of periodic (i.e. at least annual) product quality reviews (21 CFR 211.180(e)). Adequate documentation of each significant step in batch production records (21 CFR 211.188(b)). Adequate review of all production and test records, including deviations, OOS results, and audit trails, prior to releasing drug product to the market (21 CFR 211.192).
key_violations.description: 귀사 품질부서는 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22). 귀사 품질부서(QU)는 OTC 의약품의 제조, 시험, 포장, 보관, 검토 및 출하를 적절히 감독할 권한을 확립·행사하지 않았다. 귀사의 부적절한 품질 감독은 분석 및 제조 기록 검토, 조사, 그리고 CGMP 요건 준수를 보장하기 위한 품질 시스템 관리에서 중대한 결함으로 이어졌다. 예를 들어 귀사 QU는 다음을 보장하지 못했다. 제조 및 시험 기록의 적절한 문서 관리를 보장하는 적절한 절차(21 CFR 211.22(d)). 세척 절차의 적절한 밸리데이션(21 CFR 211.67(b)). 정기적(즉 최소 연 1회) 제품 품질 검토의 수행(21 CFR 211.180(e)). 배치 제조 기록의 각 중요 단계에 대한 적절한 문서화(21 CFR 211.188(b)). 의약품을 시장에 출하하기 전 일탈, OOS 결과, 감사추적을 포함한 모든 제조 및 시험 기록의 적절한 검토(21 CFR 211.192).
key_violations.risk: QU 가 문서관리·세척 밸리데이션·연간 품질 검토·감사추적 검토를 통제하지 못하면 개별 결함이 출하 단계에서 걸러지지 않아 시스템 전반의 품질 보증이 무너진다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 회신(2026년 5월 22일자)을 항목별로 불충분하다고 평가했다. OOS·불만 처리에 대해서는 소급 검토와 최초 OOS 결과에 대한 임시 '전면 중지' 조치를 약속했으나, OOS 결과와 불만이 항상 적절히 처리되도록 보장할 계획과 재발 방지를 위한 지속 가능한 시정 세부 내용이 없다고 지적했다. 시험실 관리에 대해서는 부실한 분석 관행의 범위를 인식하지 못했고 개별 분석법 개정·교육·OOS 무효화 관행의 시스템적 시정을 다루지 않았으며, 과거 약속도 효과가 없었다고 보았다. 원료 시험에 대해서는 절차 개선·시험 내용·축소 시험 전략의 세부가 부족하고 원료 보관검체 평가를 약속하지 않았다고 평가했다. 또한 2022년 4월 1일 규제 회의에서 유사한 CGMP 위반을 지적했음에도 반복된 점을 들어 경영진의 감독이 부적절하다고 판단했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서신 수령 후 15영업일 이내 CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov 로 서면 회신(FEI 3009188709 명기)
items: 일탈·불만·OOS 조사 시스템 전반에 대한 독립적 종합 평가와 상세 시정 계획, 미국 내 유통 중인 유효기간 내 제품의 무효화된 OOS 결과 전건에 대한 독립적 소급 검토 보고서 제출
최근 3년간 전체 불만에 대한 소급 검토를 포함한 불만 시스템의 독립적 종합 검토와 CAPA 프로그램의 독립적 평가·시정 계획 제출
시험실 관행·절차·방법·장비·분석자 역량의 독립적 평가, 유효기간 내 미국 유통 전 배치의 보관검체 화학·미생물 전항목 시험 계획과 결과 요약 제출
공급업체 적격성평가 프로그램을 포함한 자재 시스템 검토, 입고 원료 로트별 확인시험 실시 약속과 COA 신뢰성 검증 프로그램(SOP) 제출, 21 CFR 211.34 요건의 CGMP 컨설턴트를 통한 6대 시스템 감사

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 위반이 해결되지 않으면 다른 연방기관의 계약 수주가 막힐 수 있고, FDA가 수출증명서 발급을 보류할 수 있다. 또한 위반이 완전히 해결되고 CGMP 준수가 확인될 때까지 이 업체를 제조소로 기재한 신규 신청이나 변경 신청의 승인이 보류될 수 있으며, FDA는 시정 조치 완료 확인을 위해 재실사할 수 있다. 반복 위반으로 경영진 책임도 명시적으로 지적됐다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 배치 또는 그 구성 성분이 규격에 부합하지 않는 원인불명의 불일치나 부적합에 대해, 해당 배치의 출하 여부와 관계없이 철저히 조사하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.192).
귀사는 원료, 의약품 용기, 마개, 공정 중 물질, 표시자재 및 의약품이 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)의 적절한 기준에 부합함을 보증하도록 설계된, 과학적으로 타당하고 적절한 규격·표준품·검체 채취 계획·시험 절차를 포함하는 시험실 관리를 수립하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.160(b)).
귀사는 의약품 각 구성 원료의 확인을 위한 시험을 최소 1개 이상 실시하지 않았다. 또한 원료 공급업체 시험 분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 검증·확립하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) and 211.84(d)(2)).
귀사 품질부서는 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보장할 책임을 이행하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.22).

9995c30e33c0.source_text: during an inspection of your drug manufacturing facility, SnugZ USA, Inc., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3009188709, at 9258 South Prosperity Road, West Jordan, from April 27 to May 1, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). We reviewed your May 22, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail and acknowledge receipt of your subsequent correspondence. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm manufactures over-the-counter (OTC) drug products such as (b)(4) and (b)(4) , primarily distributed by your customers as promotional items. Your firm routinely failed to investigate out-of-specification (OOS) chemical and microbiological results for drug products and for (b)(4) system monitoring samples. Your firm retested failing samples or prepared and tested new samples without justification until your analysts obtained passing results. Your firm used these results to release drug product to the market without appropriate investigations into the original failing results. Additionally, your firm failed to conduct adequate complaint investigations. Your investigations consisted largely of email correspondence and lacked proper root cause determination and implementation of corrective actions and preventive actions (CAPA). Inadequate investigations are a repeat observation identified at your firm. In your response, you commit to a retrospective review of the OOS results and implemented an interim “full stop” for any initial OOS result. You also state you will review prior OOS results and customer complaints to determine product impact and ensure release decisions were scientifically justified. Your response is inadequate. You failed to provide plans on how you will ensure that OOS results and complaints are always appropriately handled. You also failed to provide adequate details of your remediations to ensure they are sustainable to prevent repeat violations. Passing retest results alone cannot serve as the basis for invalidating OOS results. As a manufacturer, you have a responsibility to fully investigate aberrant chemical and microbial test results that may impact drug product quality. For more information about handling out-of-specification and failing test results and documenting your investigations, see FDA’s guidance document Investigating Out-of-Specification (OOS) Test Results for Pharmaceutical Production at https://www.fda.gov/media/158416/download. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, OOS results, and failures. Provide a detailed action plan to remediate this system. Your action plan should include, but not be limited to, significant improvements in investigation competencies, scope determination, root cause evaluation, CAPA effectiveness, quality unit oversight, and written procedures. Address how your firm will ensure all phases of investigations are appropriately conducted. A retrospective, independent review of all invalidated OOS (including in-process and release/stability testing) results for products currently in the U.S. market and within expiry as of the date of this letter and a report summarizing the findings of the analysis, including the following for each OOS result: o Determine whether the scientific justification and evidence relating to the invalidated OOS result conclusively or inconclusively demonstrates causative laboratory error. o For investigations that conclusively establish laboratory root cause, provide rationale and ensure that all other laboratory methods vulnerable to the same or similar root cause are identified for remediation. o For all OOS results found by the retrospective review to have an inconclusive or no root cause identified in the laboratory, include a thorough review of production (e.g., batch manufacturing records, adequacy of the manufacturing steps, suitability of equipment/facilities, variability of raw materials, process capability, deviation history, complaint history, batch failure history). Provide a summary of potential manufacturing root causes for each investigation, and any manufacturing operation improvements. An independent assessment and remediation plan for your CAPA program. Provide a report that evaluates whether the program includes effective root cause analysis, ensures CAPA effectiveness, analyzes investigations trends, improves the CAPA program whenever needed, ensures final quality unit decision authority, and is fully supported by executive management. A comprehensive, independent review of your overall complaint system, including a retrospective review of all complaints for the last three years from the initial date of inspection with an assessment that includes, but is not limited to: o Nature of complaint, and potential associated risk o Date of first notification and subsequent contacts with complainant o Timing and sufficiency of follow-ups with the complainant to obtain photographs and the complaint sample, as well as to obtain any additional contextual information. Determination of whether relevant complaint samples were available and extent of efforts to obtain the complaint sample. If insufficient attempts were made, identify the root cause(s) for not adequately pursuing their return. o Review of long-term history for similar or same defects. o Identification of potential causes of the defect that led to the complaint, including evaluation of whether the scientific justification and evidence relating to the identified root cause(s) were adequately documented. In the event a complaint was attributed to factors outside of the firm’s control(e.g., user error), assess the strength of this determination and whether it was based on conclusive or inconclusive information. o CAPA steps taken including, but not limited to, manufacturing/quality improvements (e.g., manufacturing operation, raw materials, supplier, quality control), as well as recalls or heightened quality surveillance (additional testing/examinations, adding batch to stability program). o For all complaint investigations found by the retrospective review to be deficient due to insufficient root cause or CAPA, perform a thorough analysis of production (e.g., batch manufacturing records, adequacy of the manufacturing steps, suitability of equipment/facilities, variability of raw materials, process capability, deviation history, complaint history, OOS result history, batch failure history). o Based upon this independent review, provide a comprehensive assessment of the complaint system that identifies all deficiencies and needed improvements. 2. Your firm failed to establish laboratory controls that include scientifically sound and appropriate specifications, standards, sampling plans, and test procedures designed to assure that components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, labeling, and drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b)). Your test method procedures allowed multiple retesting of samples following an OOS result, often until an acceptable result is obtained. For example, your (b)(4) standard operating procedure (SOP) described repreparing OOS samples and retesting multiple times without requiring investigations. The SOP requires notifying quality control management only after (b)(4) OOS results. Your procedure also stated that if an unidentified peak is observed during chromatographic analysis, it is at the discretion of the analyst to consult the Quality Control manager to determine whether further action is needed. Additionally, your (b)(4) Microbial Testing SOP allows retesting following an initial failure. Also, your SOP says that if the retest fails, your analysts are to use the (b)(4) , a second microbiological testing instrument. You routinely invalidated failing batch release results from the (b)(4) system and used the passing (b)(4) results to release product to the market without scientific justification. You could not provide any data to support this tiered testing approach or the validation of one method as superior to the other. In your response, you commit to implementing an interim requirement to open an OOS investigation for all initial failing results. You also commit to revising your OOS procedure to define when repeat testing, re-injection, re-vialing, etc. are allowed, when Quality Assurance authorization is required, and to require scientific justification and documentation of all data generated. Your response is inadequate because it fails to recognize the scope of your poor analytical practices. You did not address revisions to specific analytical methods, training, or systemic remediation of your routine practice of invalidating OOS results and retesting. Inadequate laboratory controls have previously been observed at your firm, and your earlier commitments to correct them and prevent their recurrence were not effective. These are unscientific practices and objectionable under CGMP. Chemical and microbial release testing, an essential quality control step, is integral in preventing distribution of unsafe products. Integrity of data is fundamentally compromised when there is a failure to record or maintain complete and accurate records of test results or conditions associated with drug testing. Furthermore, the lack of reliable data compromises the Quality Unit’s (QU) ability to exercise its function of ensuring compliance with applicable standards. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive independent assessment of your laboratory practices, procedures, methods, equipment, documentation, and analyst competencies. Based on this review, provide a detailed plan to remediate and evaluate the effectiveness of your laboratory system. A list of chemical and microbial specifications, including test methods, used to analyze each batch of your drug products before a lot disposition decision. An action plan and timelines for conducting full chemical and microbiological testing of retain samples to determine the quality of all batches of drug product distributed in the United States that are within expiry as of the date of this letter. A summary of all results obtained from testing retain samples from each batch. If such testing reveals substandard quality drug products, take rapid corrective actions, such as notifying customers and product recalls. A comprehensive review and remediation plan for your OOS result investigation systems. The CAPA should include but not be limited to addressing the following: o Quality unit oversight of laboratory investigations o Identification of adverse laboratory control trends o Resolution of causes of laboratory variation o Initiation of thorough investigations of potential manufacturing causes whenever a laboratory cause cannot be conclusively identified o Adequate scoping of each investigation and its CAPA o Revised OOS investigation procedures with these and other remediations o A similar review and remediation of your system for handling out-of-limit findings (i.e., data that falls outside action limits) 3. Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product. Your firm also failed to validate and establish the reliability of your component supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) and 211.84(d)(2)). You failed to perform adequate identity testing of incoming components used in the manufacture of your OTC drug products. You also failed to collect representative samples from each lot of components. In some cases, you relied on identity test results from previously tested component lots when receiving new shipments of the same component lot. Additionally, you failed to establish the reliability of your suppliers’ certificates of analyses (COAs) at appropriate intervals and accepted COAs without confirmatory testing. In your response, you commit to revising your supplier qualification and raw material sampling SOPs. You commit to reducing testing criteria and identifying an outside laboratory to perform confirmatory testing for your suppliers’ COAs. You also commit to testing each shipment of components received prior to use. Your response is inadequate. You did not provide sufficient details about your planned procedural improvements, the testing to be performed, your strategy for reduced testing, nor did you commit to evaluating component retains. Without adequate testing and verification of supplier results, you do not have scientific evidence that your incoming components conform to appropriate specifications prior to use in the manufacture of your drugs. As a manufacturer, you have a responsibility to sample, test, and examine incoming materials before use in production to assure adequate quality. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent review of your material system including, but not limited to: o Evaluating all suppliers of materials (components, containers, and closures) to determine whether they are reliable and appropriately qualified o An assessment of all materials to determine whether they are consistently of acceptable quality o A review to ensure assigned expiration or retest dates are appropriate and supported by data o Adequacy of the supplier qualification program and its selection, qualification, and disqualification provisions. Based on a thorough review, provide a summary of your systems CAPA to remediate the vendor qualification program and prevent use of unsuitable components, containers, and closures. The chemical and microbiological quality control specifications you use to test and release each incoming lot of components for use in manufacturing. A description of how you will test each component lot for conformity with all appropriate specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity. If you intend to accept any results from your supplier’s COA instead of testing each component lot for strength, quality, and purity, specify how you will robustly establish the reliability of your supplier’s results through initial validation as well as periodic re-validation. In addition, include a commitment to always conduct at least one specific identity test for each incoming component lot. A summary of results obtained from testing all components to evaluate the reliability of the COA from each component manufacturer. Include your SOP that describes this COA validation program. A summary of your program for qualifying and overseeing contract facilities that test the components and drug products you manufacture. 4. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Your QU failed to establish and exercise its authority to adequately oversee the manufacturing, testing, packing, holding, review, and release of your OTC drug products. Your firm’s inadequate quality oversight resulted in significant deficiencies in analytical and production record review, investigations, and quality system controls to ensure compliance with CGMP requirements. For example, your QU failed to ensure: Adequate procedures ensuring appropriate document controls of production and test records. (21 CFR 211.22(d)). Adequate validation of cleaning procedures (21 CFR 211.67(b)). Performance of periodic (i.e. at least annual) product quality reviews (21 CFR 211.180(e)). Adequate documentation of each significant step in batch production records (21 CFR 211.188(b)). Adequate review of all production and test records, including deviations, OOS results, and audit trails, prior to releasing drug product to the market (21 CFR 211.192). Significant findings in this letter demonstrate that your firm does not operate an effective quality system in accord with CGMP. In addition to the lack of effective management oversight of your production and laboratory operations, we found your QU is not enabled to exercise proper authority and/or has insufficiently implemented its responsibilities. Executive management should immediately and comprehensively assess your company’s global manufacturing operations to ensure that your systems, processes, and products conform to FDA requirements. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. For help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211, see FDA’s guidance documents Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations at https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download. Repeat Violations at Facility In a previous April 1, 2022 Regulatory Meeting, FDA cited similar CGMP violations. You proposed specific remediation for these violations in your responses. Repeated failures demonstrate that executive management oversight and control over the manufacture of drugs is inadequate. CGMP Consultant Based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34 to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive six-system audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of your corrective actions and preventive actions before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. Your use of a consultant does not relieve your firm’s obligation to comply with CGMP. Your firm’s executive management remains responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure ongoing CGMP compliance. Conclusion You are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. Unresolved violations may prevent other Federal agencies from awarding contracts. Failure to address violations may also cause FDA to withhold issuance of Export Certificates. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to address any violations. Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within 15 business days of receipt of this letter. Identify your written response with FEI 3009188709 and ATTN: Compliance Officer Christina Capacci-Daniel in the letter. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. FDA posts warning letters to www.FDA.gov. Sincerely, /S/ Francis Godwin Director Office of Manufacturing Quality Office of Compliance Center for Drug Evaluation and Research U.S. Food and Drug Administration Content current as of: 10/20/2026 Regulated Product(s) Drugs Over-the-Counter Drugs Feedback FDA Archive About FDA Accessibility Visitor Information Website Policies / Privacy No FEAR Act Vulnerability Disclosure Policy FOIA HHS.gov USA.gov Contact FDA Follow FDA on Facebook Follow FDA on X Follow FDA on Instagram Follow FDA on LinkedIn View FDA videos on YouTube Subscribe to FDA RSS feeds Contact Number 1-888-INFO-FDA (1-888-463-6332) Back to Top

key_violations.original: 1. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards. Your firm also failed to clean, maintain, and, as appropriate for the nature of the drug, sanitize and/or sterilize equipment and utensils at appropriate intervals to prevent malfunctions or contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements (21 CFR 211.194(a) and 21 CFR 211.67(a)). Your firm manufactures over-the-counter (OTC) topical ophthalmic drug products using aseptic processing. Our inspection revealed systemic data falsification. Notably, we observed critical data integrity breaches in your environmental monitoring (EM), personnel monitoring (PM), and cleaning records. Falsified Environmental Monitoring Records Our inspection identified critical discrepancies in your surface monitoring records. Your standard operating procedure (SOP) required post-batch surface sampling at (b)(4) locations. Your firm acknowledged repeatedly submitting unexposed plates to the laboratory and confirmed that you did not perform the actual sampling. In other instances, only partial sampling was performed. Similarly, personnel monitoring samples were not collected for production and engineering personnel who worked in the aseptic processing room. Instead, unexposed plates were submitted to the laboratory and the associated records reflected that personnel sampling had been performed. Further, in a separate instance, active air samples for a batch were collected at incorrect locations but falsely documented as having been collected at the required locations. These falsification practices fundamentally undermine any confidence in your microbiology data. Notably, you lacked reliable data indicating that environmental control existed in your aseptic processing operations and to support release of batches to the U.S. market. During this period, you reported 0 colony-forming unit findings across all EM and PM sampling with the exception of a single deviation following a water leakage event. In stark contrast, following discussion of deficiencies with firm management, actual plate readings conducted during the inspection (April 10 to 14, 2026) yielded numerous EM and PM samples with microbial growth, including approximately 25 ISO 5 excursions.
key_violations.description: 1. 귀사는 실험실 기록이 확립된 규격 및 기준 적합성 보증에 필요한 모든 시험에서 얻은 완전한 데이터를 포함하도록 보장하지 않았다. 또한 귀사는 의약품의 안전성·확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)를 공적 또는 기타 확립된 요건을 벗어나 변화시킬 수 있는 오작동이나 오염을 방지하기 위해, 설비와 기구를 적절한 주기로 세척·유지하고 의약품 특성에 따라 적절히 소독 및/또는 멸균하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.194(a) 및 21 CFR 211.67(a)). 귀사는 무균공정으로 일반의약품(OTC) 국소 점안제를 제조한다. 실사 결과 체계적인 데이터 조작이 드러났다. 특히 환경모니터링(EM), 작업자 모니터링(PM), 세척 기록에서 중대한 데이터 무결성 위반을 관찰했다. [환경모니터링 기록 조작] 실사에서 표면 모니터링 기록의 중대한 불일치가 확인됐다. 귀사 표준작업절차서(SOP)는 배치 종료 후 (비공개) 개 위치에서 표면 검체를 채취하도록 요구했다. 귀사는 노출되지 않은 배지를 반복적으로 실험실에 제출했고 실제 검체 채취를 수행하지 않았음을 인정했다. 다른 경우에는 일부만 채취했다. 마찬가지로 무균공정실에서 작업한 생산·엔지니어링 인원에 대한 작업자 모니터링 검체도 채취되지 않았다. 대신 노출되지 않은 배지가 실험실에 제출됐고, 관련 기록에는 작업자 검체 채취가 수행된 것으로 기재됐다. 또한 별도 사례로, 한 배치의 능동 공기 검체가 잘못된 위치에서 채취됐는데도 규정 위치에서 채취한 것처럼 허위 기록됐다. 이러한 조작 관행은 귀사 미생물 데이터에 대한 신뢰를 근본적으로 훼손한다. 특히 귀사는 무균공정 운영에 환경 관리가 존재했음을 보여주고 미국 시장 배치 출하를 뒷받침할 신뢰할 수 있는 데이터가 없었다. 이 기간 동안 귀사는 누수 사건 이후의 단일 일탈을 제외하고 모든 EM·PM 검체에서 집락형성단위(CFU) 0을 보고했다. 이와 극명히 대조적으로, 업체 경영진과 결함을 논의한 후 실사 기간(April 10 to 14, 2026) 중 실시한 실제 배지 판독에서는 약 25건의 ISO 5 이탈을 포함해 다수의 EM·PM 검체에서 미생물 증식이 확인됐다.
key_violations.risk: 환경·작업자 모니터링 데이터가 조작돼 무균 보증 근거가 사라졌고, 실제 판독에서 ISO 5 이탈이 다수 확인돼 이미 미국에 출하된 점안제의 무균성 자체가 의심된다.

key_violations.original: Falsified Cleaning Records Your SOP required cleaning ISO 5 surfaces (b)(4) decontamination of the room. Although cleaning records documented that these activities were completed on January 23, January 30, March 10, and March 21, 2026, our inspection found no evidence that the cleaning activities were performed. Your management confirmed that the documented cleaning activities were not performed and that the records reported false information.
key_violations.description: [세척 기록 조작] 귀사 SOP는 ISO 5 표면 세척과 (비공개) 실(room) 제염을 요구했다. 세척 기록에는 이 활동이 January 23, January 30, March 10, and March 21, 2026에 완료된 것으로 기재돼 있었으나, 실사에서는 세척 활동이 수행됐다는 증거를 찾지 못했다. 귀사 경영진은 기록된 세척 활동이 수행되지 않았으며 해당 기록이 허위 정보를 담고 있음을 확인했다.
key_violations.risk: 수행되지 않은 ISO 5 세척·제염이 완료로 기록돼 무균 구역 오염 관리의 실체가 없었고, 세척 기록 전반의 신뢰성이 무너진다.

key_violations.original: 2. Your firm failed to establish and follow appropriate written procedures that are designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile, and that include validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes. Your firm also failed to use equipment in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of drug products that is of appropriate design, adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use and for its cleaning and maintenance (21 CFR 211.113(b) and 21 CFR 211.63). Your firm failed to adequately design, control, and supervise your aseptic processing line. Poor Aseptic Practices and Cleanroom Behavior We observed numerous poor aseptic practices across multiple batches, operators, and dates during the manufacture of U.S.-marketed ophthalmic drug products including, but not limited to, the following: A gowned operator stood inside the ISO 5 area near the (b)(4) , picking up exposed open sterile bottles with (b)(4) and reintroducing them into the bottle supply rather than rejecting them. Operators repeatedly used (b)(4) directly above and in contact with open bottles and critical surfaces during undocumented interventions without rejecting the exposed containers.
key_violations.description: 2. 귀사는 무균으로 표시되는 의약품의 미생물 오염을 방지하도록 설계되고 모든 무균 및 멸균 공정의 밸리데이션을 포함하는 적절한 문서화된 절차를 수립·준수하지 않았다. 또한 귀사는 의약품의 제조·가공·포장·보관에 의도된 용도와 세척·유지에 적합하도록 적절한 설계·충분한 크기·적절한 위치의 설비를 사용하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.113(b) 및 21 CFR 211.63). 귀사는 무균공정 라인을 적절히 설계·관리·감독하지 않았다. [부적절한 무균 작업 및 청정실 행동] 미국 판매용 점안제 제조 중 여러 배치·작업자·일자에 걸쳐 다수의 부적절한 무균 작업을 관찰했으며, 다음을 포함하나 이에 국한되지 않는다. 무균복을 착용한 작업자가 ISO 5 구역 안 (비공개) 근처에 서서, 노출된 개봉 상태의 멸균 용기를 (비공개)(으)로 집어 폐기하지 않고 용기 공급부에 다시 투입했다. 작업자들은 기록되지 않은 개입 중 개봉 용기와 중요 표면 바로 위에서, 또한 이에 접촉한 채로 (비공개)을(를) 반복 사용하면서 노출된 용기를 폐기하지 않았다.
key_violations.risk: ISO 5 내 개봉 멸균 용기 재투입·미기록 개입은 제품 직접 오염 경로로, 점안제의 무균성을 보증할 수 없게 한다.

key_violations.original: 3. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm failed to adequately investigate out-of-limit 100% visual inspection findings for two batches of sterile ophthalmic drug products that exceeded the (b)(4) % total reject limit. Rather than conducting a full 100% re-inspection, only (b)(4) units per batch were re-inspected, and the investigations did not characterize the nature, composition, or source of the particles. Both batches were released and shipped to the U.S. market without determining whether the particles were intrinsic, extrinsic, or inherent.
key_violations.description: 3. 귀사는 배치가 이미 유통됐는지 여부와 관계없이, 설명되지 않은 불일치나 배치 또는 그 구성 성분의 규격 부적합을 철저히 조사하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.192). 귀사는 (비공개)% 총 불량 한도를 초과한 무균 점안제 두 배치의 100% 육안검사 한도 초과 결과를 적절히 조사하지 않았다. 100% 전수 재검사를 하지 않고 배치당 (비공개) 개만 재검사했으며, 조사에서는 이물의 성상·조성·출처를 규명하지 않았다. 두 배치 모두 이물이 내재성(intrinsic)·외래성(extrinsic)·고유성(inherent) 중 무엇인지 판단하지 않은 채 출하돼 미국 시장으로 선적됐다.
key_violations.risk: 출처 불명의 이물이 있는 점안제가 출하돼 소비자가 유해 입자를 눈에 점적할 위험이 있으며, 외래 이물은 미생물 오염 가능성을 시사할 수 있다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 May 1, 2026 자 Form FDA 483 회신을 상세히 검토했다. 업체는 미국향 생산 중단·유통 중지 통보, 기록 조작 인정, 관련 인원 직무 정지와 독립 제3자 평가 착수를 밝혔으나, FDA는 조작된 EM 데이터는 추세 분석에 쓸 수 없으므로 이를 근거로 한 초기 제품 영향평가는 뒷받침될 수 없고, 다수 인원·다수 기록 유형·장기간에 걸친 조작이라는 체계적 범위와 고위 경영진의 책임 불이행을 충분히 인정하지 않았다고 판단했다. 무균 작업 결함 회신은 범위와 근본 원인을 다루지 않아, 이물 조사 회신은 이물 출처가 미결이고 부정적 품질 추세에도 배치를 출하한 결정을 설명하지 않아 각각 부적절하다고 평가했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 본 서한에 대한 회신으로 FDA가 열거한 평가·CAPA 자료를 제출(In response to this letter, provide)
items: 실험실 체계·문서화 체계에 대한 포괄적 독립 평가와, 기록이 동시적·귀속 가능·판독 가능·완전·원본·정확(ALCOA)하도록 하는 CAPA 계획 제출
자격 있는 컨설턴트 감독하에 미생물 검체의 고유 라벨링·취급자 서명·시각 기록·배지 디지털 타임스탬프 사진 등 완전한 관리연속성(custody)·대사 체계 구축
ISO 5 내 인적 개입·설비 적합성·기류·시설 배치·인원/물자 동선·소독을 포함한 오염 위해 독립 위험평가, 동적 조건의 기류 시각화(smoke study) 재실시 및 개선 일정 제출
일탈·불만·OOS·한도 초과 조사 체계와 100% 육안검사 프로그램(결함 분류·한도, 검사 시스템 적격성 평가 등)에 대한 독립 평가와 개선 계획 제출

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: FDA는 해당 업체의 의약품이 FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B)에 따른 불량의약품(adulterated)이고, ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops 제품군이 505(a)상 미승인 신약이자 502(a)·502(ee)상 부정표시(misbranded) 제품이며, 이를 주간 상거래에 도입하는 것이 301(d)·(a)로 금지된다고 명시했다. 업체는 이미 미국향 생산을 중단했으며, 시정이 불충분하면 미국 시장 공급 중단 상태가 길어질 수 있다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 실험실 기록이 확립된 규격 및 기준 적합성 보증에 필요한 모든 시험에서 얻은 완전한 데이터를 포함하도록 보장하지 않았다. 또한 의약품의 안전성·확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)를 공적 또는 기타 확립된 요건을 벗어나 변화시킬 수 있는 오작동이나 오염을 방지하도록 설비와 기구를 적절한 주기로 세척·유지하고, 의약품 특성에 따라 적절히 소독 및/또는 멸균하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.194(a) and 21 CFR 211.67(a)).

귀사는 무균으로 표시되는 의약품의 미생물 오염을 방지하도록 설계되고 모든 무균 및 멸균 공정의 밸리데이션을 포함하는 적절한 문서화된 절차를 수립·준수하지 않았다. 또한 의약품의 제조·가공·포장·보관에 의도된 용도와 세척·유지에 적합하도록 적절한 설계·충분한 크기·적절한 위치의 설비를 사용하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.113(b) and 21 CFR 211.63).
귀사는 배치가 이미 유통됐는지 여부와 관계없이, 설명되지 않은 불일치나 배치 또는 그 구성 성분의 규격 부적합을 철저히 조사하지 않았다 (21 CFR 211.192).

e68818062d22.source_text: during an inspection of your drug manufacturing facility, Rohto-Mentholatum (Vietnam) Co., Ltd., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3008808745, at No. 16 VSIP Street No. 5, Vietnam - Singapore Industrial Park, Thuan Giao Ward, Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam, from April 6 to 14, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). In addition, violations were identified and documented during a review of your product labeling and website at the internet address https://rohtoeyedrops.com/ and your Instagram account at https://www.instagram.com/rohtoeyedrops/ in August 2026. Based on our review, your “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops COOL RELIEF,” “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops ALL-IN-ONE,” “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops MAX STRENGTH,” “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops DIGI EYE,” “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops OPTIC GLOW,” “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops DRY AID,” and “ROHTO® Cooling Eye Drops DUAL LIGHT RELIEF” are unapproved new drugs under section 505(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 355(a). In addition, these products are misbranded under sections 502(a) and 502(ee) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 352(a) and 352(ee). As explained further below, introducing or delivering these products for introduction into interstate commerce is prohibited under sections 301(d) and (a) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 331(d) and (a). We reviewed your May 1, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail and acknowledge receipt of your subsequent correspondence. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act CGMP Violations The following are violations identified during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to ensure that laboratory records included complete data derived from all tests necessary to ensure compliance with established specifications and standards. Your firm also failed to clean, maintain, and, as appropriate for the nature of the drug, sanitize and/or sterilize equipment and utensils at appropriate intervals to prevent malfunctions or contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements (21 CFR 211.194(a) and 21 CFR 211.67(a)). Your firm manufactures over-the-counter (OTC) topical ophthalmic drug products using aseptic processing. Our inspection revealed systemic data falsification. Notably, we observed critical data integrity breaches in your environmental monitoring (EM), personnel monitoring (PM), and cleaning records. Falsified Environmental Monitoring Records Our inspection identified critical discrepancies in your surface monitoring records. Your standard operating procedure (SOP) required post-batch surface sampling at (b)(4) locations. Your firm acknowledged repeatedly submitting unexposed plates to the laboratory and confirmed that you did not perform the actual sampling. In other instances, only partial sampling was performed. Similarly, personnel monitoring samples were not collected for production and engineering personnel who worked in the aseptic processing room. Instead, unexposed plates were submitted to the laboratory and the associated records reflected that personnel sampling had been performed. Further, in a separate instance, active air samples for a batch were collected at incorrect locations but falsely documented as having been collected at the required locations. These falsification practices fundamentally undermine any confidence in your microbiology data. Notably, you lacked reliable data indicating that environmental control existed in your aseptic processing operations and to support release of batches to the U.S. market. During this period, you reported 0 colony-forming unit findings across all EM and PM sampling with the exception of a single deviation following a water leakage event. In stark contrast, following discussion of deficiencies with firm management, actual plate readings conducted during the inspection (April 10 to 14, 2026) yielded numerous EM and PM samples with microbial growth, including approximately 25 ISO 5 excursions. Falsified Cleaning Records Your SOP required cleaning ISO 5 surfaces (b)(4) decontamination of the room. Although cleaning records documented that these activities were completed on January 23, January 30, March 10, and March 21, 2026, our inspection found no evidence that the cleaning activities were performed. Your management confirmed that the documented cleaning activities were not performed and that the records reported false information. The profound data integrity breaches at your firm critically undermined assurance of sterility for U.S.-distributed drug products. In your response, you state that you suspended drug production for the U.S. market and notified your U.S. distributor of the need to halt distribution. You acknowledge that EM, PM, and cleaning records were falsified. You note several root causes, including a lack of independent oversight by quality assurance personnel and insufficient real-time supervision of cleaning execution. You state that you suspended all personnel involved and engaged an independent third-party to assess the scope of the data integrity issues. Notably, throughout your response, you reference your historical viable EM data, citing the absence of adverse trends, as a key “quality indicator data” source to support your initial product impact assessment. Your response is inadequate. Falsified EM data cannot be used for trending analysis. Therefore, your initial product impact assessment is not supportable as it relies on EM data confirmed to be unreliable. Furthermore, you have not sufficiently acknowledged the potential scope of the systemic data integrity breaches, which extended well beyond procedural gaps or individual misconduct. Widespread falsification across many staff members, multiple record types, and over an extended period of time went unchecked, reflecting a systemic quality failure and demonstrating a general failure of senior managers in your company to exercise their responsibility to ensure integrity of manufacturing and laboratory records. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent assessment of your laboratory practices, procedures, methods, equipment, documentation, supervisory oversight, and analyst competencies. Based on this review, provide a detailed plan to remediate and evaluate the effectiveness of your laboratory system. A comprehensive, independent assessment of documentation systems used throughout your manufacturing and laboratory operations to determine where documentation practices are insufficient. Include a detailed corrective action and preventive action (CAPA) plan that comprehensively remediates your firm’s documentation practices to ensure you retain contemporaneous, attributable, legible, complete, original, and accurate records throughout your operation. A comprehensive CAPA, overseen by a qualified consultant, for handling microbiological sampling media to ensure robust and reliable data. Establish a system that ensures uncompromised and uninterrupted custody, with full reconciliation of all microbiological samples including, but not limited to, the following: o Unique labeling of each sample o Signatures of all staff who handle the sample o Complete tracking of uncompromised sample integrity and custody o Date and time of each activity (e.g., sample collection, transport, delivery, incubation, removal from incubator) o Digital time-stamped photos of all plates o Laboratory tools and methods to optimize visibility and detectability of colonies on plates o Signatures of personnel performing reading of microbial counts o Provisions for verifications and routine quality assurance oversight An independent assessment and remediation plan for your CAPA program. Provide a report that evaluates whether the program includes effective root cause analysis, ensures CAPA effectiveness, analyzes investigations trends, improves the CAPA program whenever needed, ensures final quality unit (QU) decision authority, and is fully supported by executive management. An independent review of your antimicrobial effectiveness testing (AET) program, including assuring that all (b)(4) products are evaluated using sound AET study protocols and that each formulation is suitable throughout its use period. A comprehensive assessment and CAPA, overseen by a qualified consultant, for your cleaning and disinfection program. Establish a system that ensures robust cleaning and disinfection and full verification and reconciliation of all related activities, including, but not limited to, provisions for meaningful independent verifications of cleaning and disinfection execution (using appropriate methods at required locations and frequencies) and effective routine quality assurance oversight. 2. Your firm failed to establish and follow appropriate written procedures that are designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile, and that include validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes. Your firm also failed to use equipment in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of drug products that is of appropriate design, adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use and for its cleaning and maintenance (21 CFR 211.113(b) and 21 CFR 211.63). Your firm failed to adequately design, control, and supervise your aseptic processing line. Poor Aseptic Practices and Cleanroom Behavior We observed numerous poor aseptic practices across multiple batches, operators, and dates during the manufacture of U.S.-marketed ophthalmic drug products including, but not limited to, the following: A gowned operator stood inside the ISO 5 area near the (b)(4) , picking up exposed open sterile bottles with (b)(4) and reintroducing them into the bottle supply rather than rejecting them. Operators repeatedly used (b)(4) directly above and in contact with open bottles and critical surfaces during undocumented interventions without rejecting the exposed containers. Operators removed partially used open sterile (b)(4) packaging component bags from the ISO 5 area following batch manufacture, stored in the ISO 7 area for up to (b)(4) , and reintroduced to future batches without following appropriate practices to ensure the contents remained sterile. These interventions were not documented in the batch record. Many interventions occurred in the (b)(4) area where equipment, including the (b)(4) and conveyer, directly contacted sterile open bottles. Despite the frequency of (b)(4) interventions in this area, you only performed infrequent decontamination (e.g., (b)(4) ) of the sterile (b)(4) area of the aseptic processing line. In addition, we observed multiple deficiencies in aseptic processing operator gowning. These and other inspectional findings indicated a lack of adequate supervisory oversight of your aseptic processing operations. Inadequate Equipment Design We also noted equipment design deficiencies and a lack of unidirectional airflow. For example, the position of the (b)(4) obstructed unidirectional airflow to the sterile (b)(4) in the (b)(4) , leading to inadequate ISO 5 protection of sterile (b)(4) packaging components. Your aseptic manufacturing processes should be designed, and operations executed, to prevent contamination hazards to your sterile product. Flaws in the design of cleanrooms and aseptic processing lines, or improper execution of aseptic operations, can promote influx of contamination into the critical processing area. These significant deviations in aseptic processes and disinfection are a further indication of insufficient control of aseptic processing operations to assure drug product sterility. In your response, you state that operator practices did not consistently align with your procedures, and that you will be remediating your qualification program for both operators and direct supervisors. You also acknowledge deficiencies in your smoke studies. To help address these deficiencies, you commit to engaging independent third-party experts to assess your operation, including aseptic practices. You also commit to conducting all future smoke studies using a qualified, neutrally buoyant smoke agent and to implementing corrective actions, including potential design modifications, based on the outcome of airflow evaluation. Your response also commits to working with the vendor to ensure the entire ISO 5 (grade A) zone for the sterile product can be decontaminated (b)(4) . Your response is inadequate because it does not adequately address the scope and root cause of the poor aseptic practices observed. See FDA’s guidance document Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing—Current Good Manufacturing Practice to help you meet the CGMP requirements when manufacturing sterile drugs using aseptic processing at https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent risk assessment of all contamination hazards with respect to your aseptic processes, equipment, and facilities, including but not limited to, the following: o All human interactions within the ISO 5 area (e.g., risk reduction or elimination of (b)(4) interventions wherever possible) o Equipment suitability (e.g., reliability, capability, ergonomics, placement) and sufficient cleanroom space o Air quality in the ISO 5 area and surrounding room including, but not limited to, air volume and flow o Facility layout o Personnel flow and material flow (movement throughout all rooms used to conduct and support sterile operations, and all material transfers) o Disinfection practices and procedures o Specific CAPA recommendations that will comprehensively address the design and control hazards identified in the risk assessment A detailed remediation plan with timelines to address the findings of the contamination hazards risk assessment. Describe specific tangible improvements to be made to aseptic processing operation design and control at your facility and explain how CAPA plan will robustly remediate your deficient sterile manufacturing operations. Include comprehensive changes to the design of both your aseptic processing lines and cleanrooms. Also, describe your plans for qualification and validation of your extensively remediated operations. Your systematic plan to assure adherence to appropriate aseptic practices, cleanroom behavior, and written procedures, including but not limited to an independent assessment of the following with accompanying CAPA: o Suitability of actual practices based on extensive retrospective review and prospective observation of aseptic processing operations o Deficiencies in production management oversight and identification of specific improvements to ensure effective and routine supervisory oversight for all batches o Frequency and depth of QU oversight (e.g., audit, ad hoc, daily interactions) of aseptic processing and its support operations o Adequacy of written procedures and operational ergonomics o The assessment should also evaluate how poor aseptic technique and cleanroom behavior may have affected the quality and sterility of your drugs. Perform a critical evaluation of airflow unidirectionality in your aseptic process with the assistance of a qualified consultant. Ensure smoke studies are conducted under dynamic conditions with thorough and complete evaluations of aseptic processing line airflow unidirectionality, including the impact of dynamic interactions and aseptic interventions. These thorough smoke studies should be performed after you remediate your aseptic operation and conducted using proper practices, including neutrally buoyant media, to appropriately visualize airflow. Your CAPA plan to implement routine, vigilant operations management oversight of facilities and equipment. This plan should ensure, among other things, prompt detection of equipment/facilities performance issues, effective execution of repairs, adherence to appropriate preventive maintenance schedules, timely technological upgrades to the equipment/facility infrastructure, enhanced production floor supervision, and improved systems for ongoing management review. A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function, that includes, but is not limited to, the following: o A determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and appropriate o Provisions for QU oversight throughout your operations to ensure satisfactory procedures and adherence to appropriate practices o A complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o Oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products o Also, describe how executive management will support robust quality assurance at your firm, including but not limited to timely provision of resources that enable proactive detection and resolution of emerging manufacturing/quality issues to assure a continuing state of control. 3. Your firm failed to thoroughly investigate any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch or any of its components to meet any of its specifications, whether or not the batch has already been distributed (21 CFR 211.192). Your firm failed to adequately investigate out-of-limit 100% visual inspection findings for two batches of sterile ophthalmic drug products that exceeded the (b)(4) % total reject limit. Rather than conducting a full 100% re-inspection, only (b)(4) units per batch were re-inspected, and the investigations did not characterize the nature, composition, or source of the particles. Both batches were released and shipped to the U.S. market without determining whether the particles were intrinsic, extrinsic, or inherent. Ophthalmic products operations should be designed to prevent particle contamination and to protect consumers from the risk of instilling potentially harmful particles into the eye. In addition, when categorizing any visible particles, extrinsic or foreign matter should receive special attention, as it may indicate possible microbial contamination. Microbes introduced directly into the eye can pose a serious risk to consumers. Irreversible damage, including partial vision loss or blindness, can occur and, in some cases, may progress to life-threatening systemic infection. In your response, you acknowledge that your investigations were inadequate and that samples sent to an external laboratory for Fourier-Transform Infrared spectroscopic analysis could not conclusively determine the composition or source of the particles. While you identified a statistical correlation between high reject rates lots and a specific (b)(4) container supplier, the particle source(s) was not confirmed through analytical testing. Your response is inadequate. The identification of particles and their sources remained inconclusive and incomplete at the time of your initial response. Your response also did not address your decision to release batches despite your significant adverse quality defect trends. A substantial number of consumer complaints have been received since 2019, including reports of leakage, burning and stinging sensation, worsening eye redness, blurry vision, and reports of foreign matter or “floating matter.” Your firm recorded "no need" or “NA” for corrective action for those customer complaints. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, out-of-specification results, out-of-limit results, and failures. Provide a detailed action plan to remediate this system. Your action plan should include, but not be limited to, significant improvements in investigation competencies, scope determination, root cause evaluation, CAPA effectiveness, QU oversight, and written procedures. Address how your firm will ensure all phases of investigations are appropriately conducted. A comprehensive, independent assessment and remediation plan for your visual inspection program to ensure compliance with CGMP. The assessment and remediation should include, but not be limited to, the following: o Implementing enhancements to your 100% visible inspection program, including defining critical, major, and minor defects and the individual defect limits for drug products. o Ensuring adequate methods, equipment, and personnel qualifications to reproducibly detect visible particulates, including particulates historically found in your operation. o Conducting rigorous qualification studies to ensure your (b)(4) visible particulate inspection systems consistently and reproducibly detect the variety of visible particulates encountered in your drug products. o Implementing destructive testing and other advanced technologies (e.g., (b)(4) ) as appropriate, with statistically significant sample sizes, for drug products that are difficult to inspect (e.g., (b)(4) containers). o Incorporating product-specific knowledge, process experience, deviation investigation analysis, recall/complaint data, and quality risk management to improve the visual inspection program. o Remediating your visual inspection program, including establishing new written procedures, equipment, and methods. Include a summary of the review and recommendations made by your independent consultant. The following are violations identified during our review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations that may exist in connection with your products or operations. 적용법령: ❍ 위반 근거 
   - ｢약사법｣ 제34조의2제1항제1호, ｢의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙｣ 제34조제1항제2호 및 ｢의약품 등 임상시험 실시기관 지정에 관한 규정｣ 제3조
key_violations.description: 처분 사유인 지정요건 미달은 임상시험 실시기관 지정 규정 제3조와 ｢의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙｣ 제34조제1항제2호에 연결되어, 기관 지정 시 요구되는 요건을 처분 시점에 충족하지 못한 것으로 판단되었다.
key_violations.risk: 지정 이후 요건 유지 관리가 미흡하면 해당 기관에서 수행된 임상시험의 의뢰자와 피험자 모두에게 영향이 미칠 수 있다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 업무정지 1개월(2026.10.21.~2026.11.20.), 1차로 확정되었고 최종처분일자는 20261021이다. 처분 근거로 ｢약사법｣ 제76조의2제1항제3호, ｢의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙｣ 제95조, [별표 8] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제49호라목이 적용되었으며, '1차' 표기로 보아 해당 개별기준의 1차 위반 처분 수위가 적용된 것이다.

required_remediation.deadline: 업무정지 기간 2026.10.21.~2026.11.20.(1개월) 동안 임상시험실시기관 업무 정지 이행
items: 처분 기간(2026.10.21.~2026.11.20.) 동안 임상시험실시기관으로서의 업무를 중단한다.
｢의약품 등 임상시험 실시기관 지정에 관한 규정｣ 제3조의 지정요건 중 미달된 항목을 보완해 요건 충족 상태를 회복한다.
진행 중이던 임상시험의 의뢰자와 업무정지 기간 중 시험 운영 방안을 협의한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 이번 처분은 [별표 8] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제49호라목에 따른 1차 처분이므로, 지정요건 미달이 해소되지 않거나 같은 위반이 반복되면 같은 기준의 차수에 따라 더 무거운 처분으로 이어질 수 있다. 처분 사실은 공개종료일자 20270220까지 공개된다.

key_violations.original:
○ 의약품 수입자의 준수사항 등의 규정 위반
 - 의약품 수입업자는「약사법」제42조제5항, 제9항 및「의약품안전규칙」제60조제2항제1호에 따라, 의약품의 품질검사를 철저히 하고 합격한 제품만을 판매하여야 하나,
 - 동 업체는 ‘옴나리스나잘스프레이(미분화시클레소니드)(제조번호:128733)’의 품질검사 승인 이전에 출하승인하여 제품을 출하한 사실이 있음
  ※ (품질검사 승인일) 2025.11.6. / (출하 승인일) 2025.10.22.
key_violations.description: 의약품 수입업자는 품질검사를 철저히 하고 합격한 제품만 판매해야 하나, 에스케이케미칼(주)는 옴나리스나잘스프레이(미분화시클레소니드)(제조번호:128733)를 품질검사 승인(2025.11.6.) 이전인 2025.10.22.에 출하승인하여 제품을 출하했다. 즉 시험 합격이 확정되기 전에 해당 제조번호가 시장에 나갔다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 대상품목 옴나리스나잘스프레이(미분화시클레소니드)(허가번호: 제5140호)에 대한 해당 품목 수입업무정지 3개월(2026. 11. 4. ~ 2027. 2. 3.)이다. 위반 근거는 「약사법」제42조제5항, 제9항 및「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」제60조제2항제1호이며, 처분 수위는 「약사법」제76조 및「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」제95조 관련 [별표8]Ⅱ.개별기준 제25호가목에 따라 정해졌다. 처분은 업체 전체가 아니라 해당 품목에 한정된다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 해당 품목(‘현진목단피’, ‘현진구기자’)에 대한 제조업무정지 3개월(2026. 11. 3. ~ 2027. 2. 2.)이다. 위반 근거는 「약사법」제62조제11호이며, 처분 근거로 「약사법」제76조제1항제4호, 제5호의17, 제3항 및 「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」제95조 관련 [별표 8] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제39호 라목 11)이 적용되었다. 최종처분일자는 20261013이다. 처분이 업체 전체가 아니라 부적합 판정을 받은 두 품목에 한정된 품목 단위 정지라는 점이 특징이다.

required_remediation.deadline: 해당 품목 제조업무정지 기간 2026. 11. 3. ~ 2027. 2. 2. 동안 ‘현진목단피’, ‘현진구기자’ 제조 중지
items: 정지 기간 중 ‘현진목단피’, ‘현진구기자’의 제조를 중단하고 그 이행 사실을 기록으로 남긴다.
부적합 제조번호(26049-01, 26027-01)에 사용된 원료 생약의 입고 시험 결과와 출하 시험 결과를 재검토해 카드뮴·뷰프로페진 기준 초과의 원인을 조사한다.
목단피 원료의 중금속(카드뮴), 구기자 원료의 잔류농약(뷰프로페진) 시험이 입고·출하 단계 시험 항목에 포함되어 있는지 확인하고 필요 시 보완한다.
동일 원료 로트를 사용한 다른 제조번호의 품질 영향 여부를 평가한다.

key_violations.risk: 허가되지 않은 원료 제조소 산 주성분이 사용된 제품이 유통되어, 불순물 프로파일·품질 동등성이 검증되지 않은 제품이 환자에게 공급될 수 있다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 처분은 수입 의약품 ‘베타딘드라이파우더스프레이’에 대한 수입업무정지 1개월이며, 이를 갈음해 과징금 1,500,000원이 부과됐다. 처분 수위는 「약사법」제76조 및 「의약품 등의 안전에 관한 규칙」 제95조 관련 [별표 8] Ⅰ. 일반기준 제8호 라목, Ⅱ. 개별기준 제5호 라목에 따른 것이고, 과징금 전환은 「약사법」제81조 및 같은 법 시행령 제33조 관련 [별표 2] 과징금 산정기준을 근거로 한다. 최종처분일자는 20261015이다.

required_remediation.deadline: 최종처분일자 20261015 — 수입업무정지 1개월 처분을 갈음한 과징금 1,500,000원 부과
items: 부과된 과징금 1,500,000원을 납부 고지에 따라 납부한다.
해당 품목의 주성분 제조원 소재지 변경 사항에 대해 「약사법」제42조제1항에 따른 변경허가 절차를 밟아 허가사항과 실제 제조소를 일치시킨다.
허가받은 제조소와 다른 제조소에서 제조된 주성분을 사용한 제품의 추가 수입·판매를 중단하고 재고·유통 현황을 점검한다.
다른 수입 품목에 대해서도 허가된 주성분 제조원과 실제 공급 제조소의 일치 여부를 점검한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 이번 처분의 수위는 [별표 8] 일반기준 제8호 라목·개별기준 제5호 라목에 근거하므로, 같은 유형의 위반이 반복되면 같은 행정처분 기준에 따라 과징금 전환이 아닌 수입업무정지 등 더 무거운 처분으로 이어질 수 있다. 처분 사실은 공개종료일자 20270328까지 공개되어 대외 신뢰에도 영향을 준다.

○ ｢마약류 관리에 관한 법률｣ 제11조 및 같은 법 시행규칙 제21조에 따라 마약류취급자는 마약류의 수출입․제조․판매․양수․양도․구입․사용․폐기 등 모든 취급내역을 마약류통합관리시스템을 통해 보고기한 내 식품의약품안전처장에게 보고하여야 함에도 불구하고,
  -  '졸피드정(졸피뎀타르타르산염)(10mg) 등 제조(변경)’ 26건에 대하여 보고기한 내 보고하지 않은 사실이 있음.
key_violations.description: 마약류취급자는 마약류의 제조 등 모든 취급내역을 마약류통합관리시스템을 통해 보고기한 내 식품의약품안전처장에게 보고해야 하나, 한미약품(주)는 '졸피드정(졸피뎀타르타르산염)(10mg) 등 제조(변경)' 26건을 보고기한 내 보고하지 않았다.
key_violations.risk: 마약류 취급내역이 적시에 보고되지 않으면 당국의 마약류 수급·유통 추적이 지연되고, 제조 기록과 보고 내역 간 불일치가 누적될 수 있다.

key_violations.original:
적용법령: ○ 「마약류 관리에 관한 법률」 제11조, 같은 법 시행규칙 제21조

key_violations.description: 처분 근거로 「마약류 관리에 관한 법률」 제11조와 같은 법 시행규칙 제21조, 그리고 같은 법 시행규칙 [별표 2] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제9호라목이 적용되었다.
key_violations.risk: 개별기준에 따른 처분이 기록으로 남아 동일 유형 위반이 반복될 경우 더 무거운 처분으로 이어질 수 있는 근거가 된다.

deep_analysis.disposition_basis: 식약처는 한미약품(주)에 (마약류제조업자) 경고 처분을 내렸다. 근거는 「마약류 관리에 관한 법률」 제11조, 같은 법 시행규칙 제21조 및 「마약류 관리에 관한 법률 시행규칙」 [별표 2] 행정처분의 기준 Ⅱ. 개별기준 제9호라목이며, 최종처분일자는 20261023이다.

required_remediation.deadline: 원문에 별도 이행기한 없음 — 최종처분일자 20261023, 공개종료일자 20270122
items: 보고기한 내 보고되지 않은 졸피드정(졸피뎀타르타르산염)(10mg) 등 제조(변경) 26건의 마약류통합관리시스템 보고 상태 확인
마약류 제조(변경) 취급내역을 보고기한 내 보고하도록 보고 절차·담당 체계 점검
제조 실적과 마약류통합관리시스템 보고 내역의 정기 대사 수행

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 이번 처분은 경고이나 「마약류 관리에 관한 법률 시행규칙」 [별표 2] 행정처분의 기준에 따른 처분 이력으로 남으며, 같은 보고 의무(제11조) 위반이 반복되면 같은 기준에 따라 더 무거운 행정처분 대상이 될 수 있다. 처분 사실은 공개종료일자 20270122까지 공개된다.
